# Hashing

Work out a hash of text.

**Library:** [Standard library](index.md#standard-library), for apps and code-pipeline hooks. More in [Cogniscript](../../../concepts/cogniscript.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`HashMd5`](#hashmd5) | Returns the MD5 hash of text, as 32 upper-case hexadecimal characters. |

### HashMd5

Returns the MD5 hash of text, as 32 upper-case hexadecimal characters.

```c
string HashMd5(string text)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | The text to hash. |

**Returns** `string`: The hash, such as `5D41402ABC4B2A76B9719D911017C592`.

`HashMd5("hello")` is `5D41402ABC4B2A76B9719D911017C592`. Pass the result to [`StringToLower`](strings.md#stringtolower) to compare it with tools that print hashes in lower case.

The text is hashed as ASCII: every character outside ASCII (an accented letter, an emoji, Arabic) is replaced by `?` first. So `café` and `cafè` hash the same, and neither matches the MD5 other tools give for that text. Use it on ASCII text only.

MD5 is not secure. Use it to spot changes or to build short keys, never for passwords or signatures.
